project.title: Initial-state matching and pressure realizability in counter-streaming electron-fluid comparisons
project.summary: Archived PIC/fluid initial-state audit, conditional loader consistency checks, receipt-bound aggregate-matching comparisons and an auxiliary continuum calibration for arXiv:2607.07106v1.
project.research_question: How do the archived physical moments differ, how sensitive are the tested fluid results to aggregate-moment matching, and which implementation, label, time and third-moment limitations remain?

claims.text: The archived initial PIC and fluid velocity moments differ: the full x-averaged moment-current profile has a relative L2 difference of 9.87 percent, and the two lower-sheet central cells differ by about 11.6 percent. Reloaded fluid output corroborates the posted initializers to roundoff.
claims.evidence_summary: Five CRC32/SHA-256 checked t=0 BP snapshots, embedded inputs byte-identical to the posted Lua decks, all 480x640 fluid cells checked, and full 640-row PIC/fluid profile comparisons; full source ZIP byte counts/MD5/SHA-256 verified separately.
claims.confidence_note: Physical moment current and velocity-covariance pressure; no native deposited-current file is identifiable. Initial mismatch percentages alone do not give a nonlinear effect or reconnection-rate bound.

claims.text: The inspected public unweighted thermal-momentum loading rule predicts a mean drift below its cold proper-velocity conversion. An unfitted quadratic-shape model provides a conditional consistency check against selected archived lower-sheet moments.
claims.evidence_summary: Complete posted PIC deck audit, pinned public loader/deposition source, converged Gaussian quadrature and independent Cartesian moment checks; conditional pointwise and shape calculations remain separate.
claims.confidence_note: Conditional on the public loading rule and stated sampling assumptions; the original executable and custom velocity-diagnostic kernel are not identified or certified.

claims.text: A specified homogeneous two-Maxwellian equilibrium stable to collisionless longitudinal electrostatic perturbations has an overstable mode in the stated finite-isotropization fluid closure.
claims.evidence_summary: Explicit rational Penrose bound, linear system, eigenvalue residual, dielectric residual and Gauss-constraint checks.
claims.confidence_note: Separate nonrelativistic continuum benchmark; no claim that this mode occurred in the source reconnection simulation or of general electromagnetic stability.

claims.text: This edition reports endpoint-admissible NUMERICAL contrasts for one_fluid_initialization_effect. All four terminal native outcomes are retained. Complete regular0-through30 saved histories are bound for every successful native completion. Native execution failures (matched_two_fluid) supply no comparison endpoint, primary metrics or complete saved-history claim. Endpoint-rejected cases (baseline_two_fluid) have no accepted primary comparison metrics. Non-PSD saved histories (baseline_one_fluid, baseline_two_fluid, matched_one_fluid) remain attached to these results. Native completion and positive-definite initial/final states do not establish physically admissible trajectories, physical causality or convergence. No rejected state is clipped, assigned a zero error or silently omitted from the outcome narrative.
claims.confidence_note: One grid and one sampled aggregate target; actual times are retained. All four native outcomes, rejected endpoint decisions and saved-history failures remain explicit; no rejected endpoint has a primary metric. Endpoint PD does not validate the saved or continuous physical trajectory. Smooth fluid labels are retained, not PIC tags. Tagged qCS is only a population-recentering contribution; central-qxxx comparisons require an unverified raw-third normalization. Only eligible endpoint pairs and eligible clean-versus-archived differences are compared.
